extracted.intended_audience: Senior Area Chairs (SACs), Area Chairs (ACs), and reviewers for NeurIPS 2019
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for senior area chairs, area chairs, and reviewers on managing the NeurIPS 2019 peer-review process: conflicts, bidding, reviewer recruitment, discussion/moderation, meta-reviews, and decision calibration. Covers operational timeline, responsibilities, and expected behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter and keep conflicts up to date
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs, ACs & reviewers must enter domain conflicts, subject areas, TPMS information, and individual conflicts in CMT within the specified windows; keep domain conflicts up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conflict entries are important for preventing conflicts during assignment. NeurIPS definitions of conflicts may change year-to-year, so read the year’s definitions carefully (linked). If you notice a conflict for an assigned submission, contact the program chairs (SACs contact program chairs; ACs contact SAC) immediately so the paper can be reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TPMS and keep your profile current
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS uses the Toronto Paper Matching System (TPMS) to help assign submissions; ACs/SACs/reviewers must log into TPMS and ensure their profile is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate TPMS profiles improve matching quality and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect deadlines and maintain reliable contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the published key dates and respond to emails promptly; ensure CMT has the correct email address and whitelist CMT emails to avoid missing communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you will be unavailable for more than a short period (e.g., during important windows like discussion or decision-making), notify your SAC/PC ASAP. NeurIPS will send most emails from CMT (email@msr-cmt.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC: oversee ACs and escalate when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SAC oversees ~7 ACs, serving as their first port of call for assistance or guidance throughout the reviewing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SACs help ACs chase late reviewers, calibrate decisions across ACs, focus on borderline papers, identify conflicts and suspicious bidding patterns, reassign submissions as needed, and discuss proposed decisions with program chairs during final decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC: identify conflicts and reassign submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs are responsible for identifying conflicts of interest (and other unusual activity such as suspicious bidding patterns) and re-assigning submissions to ACs or reviewers accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because SACs and program chairs are not blind to author identities, they must actively prevent conflicts and intervene where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC: calibrate decisions and handle borderline cases
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs should work closely with their ACs to calibrate decisions and pay particular attention to borderline papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide how best to communicate with ACs (email, phone, video conferences, etc.). SACs will discuss all proposed decisions with the PCs during finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC: oversee assigned submissions and reviewer quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each AC oversees around 20 submissions and is the principal contact for reviewers; ACs must ensure each submission has suitable, expert reviewers whose opinions they can trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is worth investing time before reviewing starts to make sure your batch has expert reviewers. If you detect a conflict, contact your SAC immediately so the paper can be reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC: recruit, recommend, and chase reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs help the program chairs recruit reviewers, recommend reviewers for submissions, and chase late reviewers throughout the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs may bid on reviewers for submissions. They should micro-adjust reviewer assignments with SACs if needed (e.g., conflicts, bad assignment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle similar/duplicate submissions carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: If two submissions are detected to be sufficiently close by the tools, reviewers will receive both and ACs will be informed; ACs must ensure the arguments to discard or accept each submission are thoroughly discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comparisons are explicit and justified in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC: initiate and moderate discussion after author response
rubrics_metrics.description: After the author response phase, ACs must initiate a discussion via CMT for each submission and ensure reviewers engage; ACs should monitor and moderate the discussion to ensure it is respectful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure your reviewers read and (if appropriate) respond to all author responses. Moderate to keep discussion civil and focused on evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC: read all reviews and evaluate review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should read all reviews carefully and evaluate their quality using the three-level scale: 'exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', or 'failed to meet expectations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use information in the reviewer instructions and how helpful the review and subsequent discussion were in making your decision. The highest-scoring reviewers may receive registration awards; low-scoring reviewers may not be invited again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers: responsibilities for reviews and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer is assigned ~4–6 submissions and is responsible for reviewing submissions, reading author responses, participating in discussions with other reviewers and ACs, and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and meta-reviews will be made public after decisions (identities remain anonymous). Reviewer identities are visible to other reviewers, ACs and SACs during the process. Reviewers will be scored and top reviewers receive registration incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the review-quality scoring system judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate the quality of each review with three scores ('exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', 'failed to meet expectations') and should apply these based on helpfulness and adherence to reviewer instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scoring affects reviewer rewards and future invitations; apply consistently and consider the review's role in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review: explain and justify decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your meta-review should explain your decision to the authors, augment the reviews, and explain how the reviews, author response, and discussion were used to arrive at your decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissing or ignoring a review is not acceptable unless you have a good reason. If you want to make a decision not clearly supported by the reviews, justify it appropriately, including reading the submission in depth and writing a detailed meta-review that explains your reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discuss assigned submissions with other SACs/ACs without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT talk to other SACs about submissions assigned to your ACs without prior approval from the program chairs, and DO NOT talk to other SACs or ACs about your own submissions or submissions with which you have a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other SACs/ACs may have conflicts; follow the chain of contact (ACs → SACs → PCs) to avoid compromising assignments or confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and resist undue influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional and listen to reviewers and ACs, but do not give in to undue influence when making decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure decisions are supported by reviews, author responses, and reasonable judgment; document justification in the meta-review if deviating from reviewers' consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify PCs/SACs if you will be significantly unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: It is acceptable to be briefly unavailable, but if you will be unavailable for more than a short period—especially during important windows like decision-making—you must inform the program chairs (or your SAC) ASAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification helps the chairs reassign duties or make contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of anonymization and public release policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of ACs and reviewers with respect to author identities (ACs cannot see author identities), but SACs and program chairs are not blind to author identities; reviewer identities are visible to other reviewers, ACs, and SACs. After decisions, reviews and meta-reviews will be made public while reviewer and SAC/AC identities remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these rules in communication and assignment; be mindful when handling conflicts and discussions because some staff can see author identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate unresolved issues to program chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter a situation you are unable to resolve on your own (e.g., conflicts, suspicious activity, assignment problems), contact the program chairs; do not use their personal emails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided program-chair contact channels to escalate and follow instructions from PCs.
